_readme: Queue written by the daily-reel-render task, drained by tools/apply_additions.py during tools/sync.bat. The task must NOT edit calendar.md or review-state.json directly - it queues here instead, and sync.bat folds these in AFTER pulling, on top of whatever the desk decided today. That is what stops the two files conflicting. Adds only: an existing calendar row (keyed on date + post title) is left exactly as the desk left it, and so is an existing review-state key - with one exception, the render flip (content: awaiting-render or rerender -> in-review, plus new revisions entries), which is what tells the desk a cut now exists. It can never write an approval; see the module docstring in tools/apply_additions.py.

scriptRevisions.changed: Initial draft, after every goal you switch ends: 4.5, 4.5.1, 4.5.2, 4.5.3. Nine scenes, three-pair shape. 4.5 is a colon lead-in carded with 4.5.1 beneath it; 4.5.2 and 4.5.3 get a card each. Hook beat rewritten after the desk flagged it as misleading. "Try it during a point and you are playing a player short." -> "Once your team signals ready for the pull, that line is locked in until the next goal." The old line attached the consequence of signalling ready early to the wrong cause; 5.3 does not permit a mid-point substitution at all. Both captions name the cut-off instead. No rule number, slide body or scene changed, so the layout is identical to v1's and was re-measured to confirm it.
Initial draft, the shape of a game: 4.2, 4.3, 6.3, 5.1.

Field tip and both captions redrafted after the desk asked about tournament time limits. The cap is now named as the event's rather than WFDF's, and the reader is sent to the format sheet. The "goals or time, whichever comes first" mechanic is deliberately not asserted: rules.json contains no time-cap rule, and that phrasing describes a hard cap where many events use a soft cap.
